hypothesis: Per the UBPR method (Saito 2020, ICTIR) and this project's own EDA (Gini=0.79 on video positive counts, pop-only baseline scoring 0.5715 vs FM's 0.6016 — popularity alone already explains a lot), reweight each positive term in the BPR loss by the inverse of an in-log-popularity-based propensity estimate (propensity(v) = (impression_count(v)/max_count)^θ, clipped), so the model is pushed to rank correctly beyond what raw popularity already predicts, rather than partly re-deriving the popularity signal already captured by the video_id embedding/pop baseline.
reflection: Last turn's research call surfaced UBPR (propensity-weighted BPR, Saito 2020) as a well-evidenced, numpy-only fix for exactly our situation (BPR-FM on a popularity-skewed implicit label) — a mechanism I haven't tried yet (all 3 tested candidates so far were negative_sampling/training_procedure/feature_addition variants that didn't touch popularity weighting itself). This is a genuinely different lever (popularity_debiasing) than anything tried, so I'll implement it directly rather than research further (budget is also down to 1, better saved).
expected_effect: nDCG@5 should move more than GAUC, since down-weighting popular-item positive pairs specifically counters popularity crowding at the top of each user's ranked list (nDCG@5 is a top-k metric most sensitive to that crowding), while GAUC (a more global pairwise measure) should move less.
